---
title: "EmploymentQuality_JobSatisfaction"
output: html_document
---
```{r Step 1: Set-Up, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# JQI JOB SATISFACTION ANALYSIS
# ============================================================
#
# Purpose:
# Examine the relationship between externally measured
# dimensions of objective employment quality and GSS
# respondents' job satisfaction.
#
# Primary dimensions:
#   1. Compensation
#   2. Benefits
#   3. Earnings stability
#
# Employment stability (JOLTS layoffs/discharges) is retained
# in the merged data but treated as supplementary.
#
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# 0. PACKAGES
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)
library(emmeans)
library(car)

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

gss_job_quality_primary <- read_csv(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)
```

```{r Step 2, Job Satisfaction Measure Construction, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# 2. CONSTRUCT JOB SATISFACTION
# ============================================================
#
# GSS satjob:
#   1 = Very satisfied
#   2 = Moderately satisfied
#   3 = A little dissatisfied
#   4 = Very dissatisfied
#
# Reverse coding produces:
#   4 = Very satisfied
#   3 = Moderately satisfied
#   2 = A little dissatisfied
#   1 = Very dissatisfied
#
# Higher values therefore indicate greater satisfaction.
#
# NOTE:
# Missing satjob values include IAP/special missing categories.
# They should not automatically be interpreted as substantive
# nonresponse.

gss_jq_satjob <- gss_job_quality_primary %>%
  mutate(
    job_satisfaction = case_when(
      satjob == 1 ~ 4,
      satjob == 2 ~ 3,
      satjob == 3 ~ 2,
      satjob == 4 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 3. BASIC DATA DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================

# Overall sample

gss_jq_satjob %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_satisfaction = sum(!is.na(job_satisfaction)),
    pct_satisfaction = mean(!is.na(job_satisfaction)) * 100
  )


# Satisfaction distribution

gss_jq_satjob %>%
  count(job_satisfaction) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100
  )


# Distribution of the original GSS variable

gss_jq_satjob %>%
  count(satjob)


# ============================================================
# 4. PRIMARY JOB-QUALITY MEASURES
# ============================================================
#
# These variables were constructed at the industry-year level
# and merged onto individual GSS respondents:
#
#   compensation
#   benefits
#   earnings_stability
#   jqi_primary_z
#
# We retain the underlying measures as well:
#
#   wage_premium
#   wage_cost_per_hour
#   benefits_nonrequired
#   earnings_volatility
#
# The primary analysis focuses on the three dimensions.

gss_jq_satjob %>%
  summarise(
    compensation_n = sum(!is.na(compensation)),
    benefits_n = sum(!is.na(benefits)),
    earnings_stability_n = sum(!is.na(earnings_stability)),
    jqi_primary_n = sum(!is.na(jqi_primary_z)),
    
    compensation_mean = mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    compensation_sd = sd(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    benefits_mean = mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    benefits_sd = sd(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    earnings_stability_mean = mean(earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    earnings_stability_sd = sd(earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    jqi_primary_mean = mean(jqi_primary_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_primary_sd = sd(jqi_primary_z, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r Step 3: Set-up of the Sample and Descriptive Statistics, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# 5. ANALYTIC SAMPLE
# ============================================================
#
# For the component analysis, require:
#   - valid job satisfaction
#   - valid compensation
#   - valid benefits
#   - valid earnings stability
#
# This gives a common sample for comparing coefficients
# across the three dimensions.

jqi_satjob <- gss_jq_satjob %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(job_satisfaction),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  )


# Sample size

jqi_satjob %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_common),
    n_industry_years = n_distinct(
      interaction(year, industry_common)
    ),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year)
  )


# ============================================================
# 6. POOLED DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
# ============================================================

jqi_satjob %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    
    satisfaction_mean = mean(job_satisfaction),
    satisfaction_sd = sd(job_satisfaction),
    
    compensation_mean = mean(compensation),
    compensation_sd = sd(compensation),
    
    benefits_mean = mean(benefits),
    benefits_sd = sd(benefits),
    
    earnings_stability_mean = mean(earnings_stability),
    earnings_stability_sd = sd(earnings_stability)
  )

```

```{r Step 4: Initial Correlations, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# 7. POOLED PEARSON CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================
#
# These provide a first descriptive comparison of the strength
# of the relationship between each objective dimension and
# subjective job satisfaction.

cor_compensation <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob$compensation,
  method = "pearson"
)

cor_benefits <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob$benefits,
  method = "pearson"
)

cor_earnings_stability <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob$earnings_stability,
  method = "pearson"
)

cor_compensation
cor_benefits
cor_earnings_stability


# ============================================================
# 8. POOLED SPEARMAN CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================
#
# Job satisfaction is an ordinal four-category measure.
# Spearman correlations therefore provide an important
# robustness check against treating the outcome as continuous.

cor_compensation_spearman <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob$compensation,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)

cor_benefits_spearman <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob$benefits,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)

cor_earnings_stability_spearman <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob$earnings_stability,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)

cor_compensation_spearman
cor_benefits_spearman
cor_earnings_stability_spearman


# ============================================================
# 9. POOLED REGRESSIONS: EACH DIMENSION SEPARATELY
# ============================================================

m_satjob_compensation <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~ compensation,
  data = jqi_satjob
)

m_satjob_benefits <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~ benefits,
  data = jqi_satjob
)

m_satjob_earnings_stability <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~ earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_satjob
)

summary(m_satjob_compensation)
summary(m_satjob_benefits)
summary(m_satjob_earnings_stability)


# ============================================================
# 10. POOLED MODEL: ALL THREE DIMENSIONS
# ============================================================
#
# This is substantively important because it asks which
# dimensions of objective employment quality are associated
# with job satisfaction conditional on the other dimensions.

m_satjob_components <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_satjob
)

summary(m_satjob_components)

cor(
  jqi_satjob$compensation,
  jqi_satjob$benefits,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cor(
  jqi_satjob$compensation,
  jqi_satjob$earnings_stability,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cor(
  jqi_satjob$benefits,
  jqi_satjob$earnings_stability,
  use = "complete.obs"
)


vif(m_satjob_components)

# Tidy coefficient table

tidy_satjob_components <- tidy(
  m_satjob_components,
  conf.int = TRUE
)

tidy_satjob_components
```

```{r Step 5: Decomposition of Different Parts of Employment Quality, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# 11. PRIMARY COMPOSITE: DESCRIPTIVE COMPARISON
# ============================================================
#
# The composite is not the primary substantive focus here.
# It is included to show how the combined measure relates
# to satisfaction compared with its individual dimensions.

jqi_satjob_composite <- gss_jq_satjob %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(job_satisfaction),
    !is.na(jqi_primary_z)
  )

m_satjob_primary_jqi <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~ jqi_primary_z,
  data = jqi_satjob_composite
)

summary(m_satjob_primary_jqi)


cor.test(
  jqi_satjob_composite$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob_composite$jqi_primary_z,
  method = "pearson"
)

cor.test(
  jqi_satjob_composite$job_satisfaction,
  jqi_satjob_composite$jqi_primary_z,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)
```

```{r Step 6: Annualized Models, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# 12. YEAR-SPECIFIC COMPONENT MODELS
# ============================================================
#
# Estimate the association separately within each GSS year.
#
# First, separate models:
#
#   satisfaction ~ compensation
#   satisfaction ~ benefits
#   satisfaction ~ earnings stability
#
# Then a joint model:
#
#   satisfaction ~ compensation +
#                   benefits +
#                   earnings stability
#
# This lets us ask whether the importance of different
# dimensions changes historically.

years_available <- sort(
  unique(jqi_satjob$year)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12A. Separate component models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

yearly_component_results <- map_dfr(
  years_available,
  function(y) {
    
    d <- jqi_satjob %>%
      filter(year == y)
    
    m_comp <- lm(
      job_satisfaction ~ compensation,
      data = d
    )
    
    m_benefits <- lm(
      job_satisfaction ~ benefits,
      data = d
    )
    
    m_earnings <- lm(
      job_satisfaction ~ earnings_stability,
      data = d
    )
    
    tibble(
      year = y,
      n = nrow(d),
      
      compensation_beta =
        coef(m_comp)[["compensation"]],
      compensation_se =
        summary(m_comp)$coefficients[
          "compensation", "Std. Error"
        ],
      compensation_p =
        summary(m_comp)$coefficients[
          "compensation", "Pr(>|t|)"
        ],
      
      benefits_beta =
        coef(m_benefits)[["benefits"]],
      benefits_se =
        summary(m_benefits)$coefficients[
          "benefits", "Std. Error"
        ],
      benefits_p =
        summary(m_benefits)$coefficients[
          "benefits", "Pr(>|t|)"
        ],
      
      earnings_stability_beta =
        coef(m_earnings)[["earnings_stability"]],
      earnings_stability_se =
        summary(m_earnings)$coefficients[
          "earnings_stability", "Std. Error"
        ],
      earnings_stability_p =
        summary(m_earnings)$coefficients[
          "earnings_stability", "Pr(>|t|)"
        ]
    )
  }
)


yearly_component_results


# Add confidence intervals

yearly_component_results <- yearly_component_results %>%
  mutate(
    compensation_ci_low =
      compensation_beta -
      qt(.975, df = n - 2) * compensation_se,
    
    compensation_ci_high =
      compensation_beta +
      qt(.975, df = n - 2) * compensation_se,
    
    benefits_ci_low =
      benefits_beta -
      qt(.975, df = n - 2) * benefits_se,
    
    benefits_ci_high =
      benefits_beta +
      qt(.975, df = n - 2) * benefits_se,
    
    earnings_stability_ci_low =
      earnings_stability_beta -
      qt(.975, df = n - 2) * earnings_stability_se,
    
    earnings_stability_ci_high =
      earnings_stability_beta +
      qt(.975, df = n - 2) * earnings_stability_se
  )


# ============================================================
# 13. YEAR-SPECIFIC JOINT MODELS
# ============================================================
#
# These models are especially important.
#
# They tell us which component is most strongly associated
# with satisfaction when the other dimensions of job quality
# are held constant.

yearly_joint_results <- map_dfr(
  years_available,
  function(y) {
    
    d <- jqi_satjob %>%
      filter(year == y)
    
    m <- lm(
      job_satisfaction ~
        compensation +
        benefits +
        earnings_stability,
      data = d
    )
    
    coefs <- tidy(
      m,
      conf.int = TRUE
    ) %>%
      filter(
        term %in% c(
          "compensation",
          "benefits",
          "earnings_stability"
        )
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        year = y,
        n = nrow(d)
      ) %>%
      select(
        year,
        n,
        term,
        estimate,
        std.error,
        statistic,
        p.value,
        conf.low,
        conf.high
      )
    
    coefs
  }
)


yearly_joint_results


# ============================================================
# 14. YEAR-SPECIFIC SPEARMAN CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================
#
# These are useful because they make fewer assumptions about
# the ordinal satisfaction outcome.

yearly_spearman_results <- map_dfr(
  years_available,
  function(y) {
    
    d <- jqi_satjob %>%
      filter(year == y)
    
    tibble(
      year = y,
      n = nrow(d),
      
      compensation_rho = cor(
        d$job_satisfaction,
        d$compensation,
        method = "spearman"
      ),
      
      benefits_rho = cor(
        d$job_satisfaction,
        d$benefits,
        method = "spearman"
      ),
      
      earnings_stability_rho = cor(
        d$job_satisfaction,
        d$earnings_stability,
        method = "spearman"
      )
    )
  }
)


yearly_spearman_results


# ============================================================
# 15. TEST WHETHER COMPONENT EFFECTS VARY BY YEAR
# ============================================================
#
# These pooled interactions provide a more formal test of
# historical variation than simply comparing separate
# year-specific coefficients.
#
# Year is treated as a factor so that we do not impose a
# linear historical trend.

m_satjob_component_year <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~
    compensation * factor(year) +
    benefits * factor(year) +
    earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_satjob
)

summary(m_satjob_component_year)


# ============================================================
# 16. JOINT TESTS OF YEAR INTERACTIONS
# ============================================================
#
# Test whether the association between each component and
# satisfaction varies across years.

m_satjob_no_comp_interaction <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~
    compensation +
    benefits * factor(year) +
    earnings_stability * factor(year) +
    factor(year),
  data = jqi_satjob
)

m_satjob_no_benefits_interaction <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~
    compensation * factor(year) +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability * factor(year) +
    factor(year),
  data = jqi_satjob
)

m_satjob_no_earnings_interaction <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~
    compensation * factor(year) +
    benefits * factor(year) +
    earnings_stability +
    factor(year),
  data = jqi_satjob
)


anova(
  m_satjob_no_comp_interaction,
  m_satjob_component_year
)

anova(
  m_satjob_no_benefits_interaction,
  m_satjob_component_year
)

anova(
  m_satjob_no_earnings_interaction,
  m_satjob_component_year
)


# ============================================================
# 17. VISUALIZATION DATA
# ============================================================
#
# Convert the yearly joint results into a convenient format
# for plotting.

plot_component_results <- yearly_joint_results %>%
  mutate(
    component = case_when(
      term == "compensation" ~ "Compensation",
      term == "benefits" ~ "Benefits",
      term == "earnings_stability" ~ "Earnings stability",
      TRUE ~ term
    )
  )

plot_component_results <- plot_component_results %>%
  mutate(
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c(
        "Compensation",
        "Benefits",
        "Earnings stability"
      )
    )
  )
# ============================================================
# 18. PLOT: COMPONENT EFFECTS BY YEAR
# ============================================================

p_component_year <- ggplot(
  plot_component_results,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = estimate,
    ymin = conf.low,
    ymax = conf.high
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    width = 0
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ component,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "fixed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Coefficient",
    title = "Dimensions of Objective Employment Quality and Job Satisfaction",
    subtitle = "Year-specific coefficients from models including all three dimensions",
    caption = "Points show coefficient estimates; bars show 95% confidence intervals."
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = c(2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014,
             2016, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024)
) +
  theme_minimal()



p_component_year


# Save figure

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "JQI_Job_Satisfaction_Component_Effects_By_Year.png"
  ),
  p_component_year,
  width = 9,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 400
)


# ============================================================
# 19. PLOT: POOLED COMPONENT COEFFICIENTS
# ============================================================

pooled_component_plot_data <- tidy(
  m_satjob_components,
  conf.int = TRUE
) %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation",
      "benefits",
      "earnings_stability"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    component = case_when(
      term == "compensation" ~ "Compensation",
      term == "benefits" ~ "Benefits",
      term == "earnings_stability" ~ "Earnings stability",
      TRUE ~ term
    )
  )


p_pooled_components <- ggplot(
  pooled_component_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = component,
    xmin = conf.low,
    xmax = conf.high
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    width = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Coefficient",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Dimensions of Objective Employment Quality and Job Satisfaction",
    subtitle = "Pooled model including compensation, benefits, and earnings stability",
    caption = "Points show coefficient estimates; bars show 95% confidence intervals."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


p_pooled_components


ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "JQI_Job_Satisfaction_Pooled_Component_Effects.png"
  ),
  p_pooled_components,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)


# ============================================================
# 20. SAVE RESULTS
# ============================================================

write_csv(
  yearly_component_results,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "jqi_job_satisfaction_yearly_separate_components.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  yearly_joint_results,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "jqi_job_satisfaction_yearly_joint_components.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  yearly_spearman_results,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "jqi_job_satisfaction_yearly_spearman.csv"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# END OF SCRIPT
# ============================================================
```
